title: Cash-side primitive discovery closed (bounded)
context: Cash-side primitive discovery opened 2026-10-06 (§25) after call- and put-side closures; operator question 'How do I get the most work out of this cash?'
evidence_at_time: Operator-journey falsification, scope reconciliation, adversarial review; [amount-redacted] multi-purpose specimen and purpose-transition specimens (§25).
rationale: No materially different cash-side operator recommendation or decision boundary found within the declared Product scope requires a new cash-specific Product primitive.
expected_consequences: Cash cases explained by existing distinctions; qualifications survive: brokerage financing in complete-state economics, coverage gaps ≠ impossibility, future-event evidence ≠ present funding; warning/recommendation/HITL/enforcement distinctions and evidence-observation loop survive.
notes: Explicitly does not ratify cash policy, optimizer, mandatory deployment, yield objective, discount rate, NPV, cash-purpose schema, strategy matrix, multi-objective precedence, Capital Protection taxonomy, lifecycle-history architecture, or implementation (81:1642-1660).

title: Product-development progression Questions → Capabilities → WW commands/BE resources → Working software → Acceptance tests, as thin vertical slice
context: Start of MVP work after primitive-discovery closures.
alternatives: horizontally designing generalized lower layers first (named as what not to do)
principal_wording: Questions → Capabilities → WW commands and BE resources → Working software → Acceptance tests
expected_consequences: Each MVP step authorizes only the next stage in the progression.
notes: Text: 'The Principal establishes the Product-development sequence'. Relation to Doc 63 capability-decomposition method not stated here.

title: MVP 1 Solution Overview: bounded RETAIN UNENCUMBERED vs SELL SHORT CALL comparison with operator-identified contract
context: First MVP slice of v2 Product after call/put/cash primitive closures.
evidence_at_time: Call-side closure distinctions (§23), 99-share specimen (§6), Growth Wheel non-automatic SELL SHORT CALL (§7).
principal_wording: The Principal ratifies this clarified MVP 1 Solution Overview and authorizes the next step in the established progression:
rationale: First executable milestone is a bounded, evidence-backed comparison, not a recommendation whose policy remains undefined (81:1715).
expected_consequences: Decision subject = account+underlying+governed quantity+Growth Wheel context; positive evidence required for unencumbered availability; semantic contract validation; NO GOVERNED PREFERENCE ESTABLISHED when policy undefined; 11 acceptance cases; explicit non-goals.
implementation: Not authorized by this decision (command/API/resource/schema/implementation excluded).
notes: Section heading says 'Clarified' overview — prior unclarified version not in repo segment.

title: MVP 1 seven minimum Product capabilities
evidence_at_time: Adversarial review; 'No missing eighth capability was demonstrated by adversarial review.'
alternatives: generic Strategy, Alternative, Recommendation, or Evidence capabilities (stated not required)
principal_wording: The Principal ratifies seven minimum Product capabilities required by the accepted MVP 1 Solution Overview:
expected_consequences: Capabilities are partial-finding questions forming a dependency graph; no global evidence gate; coherent composition required; seven has no architectural significance.
implementation: None by this step ('No command/resource discovery or implementation is performed by this ratification step.').
subsequent: §30 composes the seven into one backend 'Bounded call-entry comparison' capability boundary.

title: MVP 1 governed evaluation uses direct, typed, deterministic functions with explicit, versioned policy (no rules engine/CEL/DMN/DSL)
context: Technology direction for implementing governed evaluation of the seven capabilities.
evidence_at_time: Isolated COTS comparison of direct Java functions, CEL Java, and embedded Apache KIE DMN using synthetic policy: all three could represent tested semantics incl. partial findings and concurrent limitations.
principal_wording: Direct, typed, deterministic functions with explicit, versioned policy.
rationale: Neither CEL nor DMN currently supplies an MVP 1 requirement whose demonstrated value justifies another evaluation boundary (81:2135).
expected_consequences: Policy remains explicit and versioned (implemented, not concealed, in code); explanations project findings; replay mechanism unselected; reconsideration triggers defined for CEL, DMN/FEEL, Drools/OPA, custom DSL.
implementation: Not authorized by this decision; Java vs TypeScript and placement left open (81:2151-2172).
subsequent: Placement resolved to backend by §30.1 without changing technology choice.
notes: Not found in ADR register (docs/07c-adrs.md grep for DMN/CEL empty); COTS experiment artifact not found in repo.

title: MVP 1 authoritative governed evaluation executes within the backend authority boundary (API v2)
context: §29.8 left evaluation placement open; Doc 77 Principal mandate governs API v2.
evidence_at_time: Doc 77 mandate 'Backend owns state and business logic; clients own presentation.'
alternatives: CLI reconstructing findings from raw evidence (warned against, 81:2155)
principal_wording: Backend owns state and business logic; clients own presentation.
rationale: Placement follows from the Doc 77 Principal mandate (81:2191-2197).
expected_consequences: Client caching limited to HTTP semantics; client cache not a state store; HTTP freshness ≠ evidence fitness; fresh client recovers from backend.
implementation: Not selected (no resources, methods, schemas, storage).
notes: Principal wording quoted is the Doc 77 mandate; the §30 milestone itself is labelled 'Principal-accepted'. Tension with v1 steering 'backend must NOT produce recommendations' — see S81B-E060.

title: MVP 1 bounded backend capability proposal: 5 information responsibilities + 4 capability boundaries + 5 design-falsification obligations
context: Bounded WW command + BE-resource discovery authorized by §28.9/§29.10.
evidence_at_time: Five design attacks: CLI vs web; fresh client; concurrent observation replacement; missing working-order coverage; HTTP-only client caching.
principal_wording: The Principal accepts the bounded proposal after five design attacks. These are acceptance obligations, not executable verification claims:
rationale: Availability, feasibility, consequences, and preference are backend-derived findings, not independently maintained state (81:2224).
expected_consequences: Comparison binds one recoverable and coherent evaluation basis; acquisition separate from comparison; partial findings distinct from operation failure; v1 is reuse evidence, not v2 authority.
implementation: None selected; next step derives smallest operator invocation and natural backend resource identities.
subsequent: No later reference to call-entry comparison found in docs/code at bef03dd (surveyor grep).
notes: 'not a permanent prohibition against a later independently useful capability' (81:2224).

title: Product scope excludes household debt/financing optimization; includes brokerage financing in complete-state economics
expected_consequences: No discovery/optimization of mortgage, HELOC, vehicle, real-estate debt; margin debit/interest/collateral may belong in comparisons.
notes: Part of the ratified closure (D001); separated as a scope decision candidate. 'This is a scope boundary, not a new cash primitive.'

title: No mandatory explicit HITL choice event; evidence-bounded observation loop
context: Cash-side closure; how Wheelwright learns of operator activity.
alternatives: operator reporting an explicit 'I choose A' event (dispensed with as mandatory)
rationale: Prices, rates, time, settlement, freshness, policy, and known context can change while holdings remain identical (81:1533).
expected_consequences: Recommendation provenance, economic history, and operator disposition remain separate; issue #34 open.
notes: Part of ratified closure account per §26.11 (81:1640).
